The main differences between the two being that while Ballistae shot missile-like-bolts, were used to breach fortifications, and were operated by 4-8 operators, the X shot shorter bolts, were used as anti-personnel weapons, were more mobile and could be operated by a single soldier. The popularity of X in India began well before the country's economic liberalisation, thanks to visionary local distribution. In 1974, Om Arora—a 30-year-old ex-army drop-out—persuaded X's U.S. publisher to grant his Delhi-based Variety Book Depot exclusive distribution rights. By the 1990s, he was importing 10,000 copies of each monthly issue, making X ubiquitous alongside Tinkle and Amar Chitra Katha on Indian newsstands. ID X.

question_text: Operation Fortitude was a sub-operation under the larger Operation Bodyguard, during WWII. Launched in March 1944. senior officer and soon-to-be four star General, George S. Patton was announced to be its commanding officer. For the operation, vast quantities of "armoured vehicles", "transport craft", and "airborne units" were "assembled", generating extensive radio traffic of continual troop movements. The main areas of operation were Norway (Fortitude North), and Pas-de-Calais region of France (Fortitude South). What was the main objective of Operation Fortitude?
answer_text: Deception operation to distract Germans from Normandy

question_text: During Bob Dylan's 1998 Grammy performance of "Love Sick," a background dancer unexpectedly ripped off his shirt to reveal a cryptic two-word message, XY, and began an interpretive dance. Dylan, although visibly bewildered, continued his performance without interruption. The dancer, Michael Portnoy, was a performance artist who  later describes his message thus, "X represents dense nutritional life. Y is, obviously, an explosive destructive force. So, XY is what I think art should be: dense, transformational, explosive life". This is known as the XY incident. ID XY.

X, real name Doreen Green, is a Marvel Comics character who debuted in 1991. Her abilities include enhanced strength, speed, agility, and reflexes. She also has a 3-4 feet long, bushy tail that enhances her balance and can be used for offense or defense, retractable knuckle spikes that carve through wood, sharp claws, and oversized incisors capable of chewing solid wood or steel. X can also communicate with __________. ID X who has often taken on villains far more powerful than expected for her size and apparent lightheartedness.

X is a genre of Hindustani classical music. Its name derives from the Sanskrit words for "immovable" or "fixed," and "verse," reflecting its characteristic combination of steadfast melodic structure and poetic form. Known for its spiritual, thoughtful, and heroic themes, X features a distinctive performance style beginning with a slow, improvised melodic introduction followed by rhythmic compositions usually sung with accompaniment from traditional instruments like the pakhavaj drum. ID X.

"Who Shaves the Barber?" is the seventh episode of the first season of the FX anthology series Fargo. The title of the episode refers to a puzzle derived from X's paradox. In the puzzle, there is a barber described as the "one who shaves all those, and those only, who do not shave themselves". The question, thus, is, does the barber shave himself? The puzzle shows that an apparently plausible scenario is logically impossible. It was suggested to X as an illustration of his paradox, but he deemed it an invalid modification. ID X who was a British philosopher, logician, mathematician, and public intellectual.

X was an American cartoonist, sculptor, author, engineer, and inventor, best known for his popular cartoons depicting complicated gadgets performing simple tasks in indirect, convoluted ways. The cartoons led to the expression "X machines" to describe similar gadgets and processes. Usually, these machines consist of a series of simple unrelated devices; the action of each triggers the initiation of the next, eventually resulting in achieving a stated goal. ID X.

X was created by Niklas Zennström, Janus Friis, and four Estonian developers, and released in August 2003. It was first acquired by eBay in 2005 for $2.6 billion, and later, in 2011, Microsoft bought X for $8.5 billion. For much of its run, most of the development team and 44% of all the division's employees were in Tallinn and Tartu, Estonia. On  May 5, 2025, X was officially retired, and the website now redirects users to Microsoft ________. ID X.
